title: U Brucculinu
canon: Càlamonte, a stone village terraced into the Madonie mountains of inland Sicily, summer into autumn 1972. Sal Comparetto, 26 — 'u Bruculinu', the Brooklyn one — butcher's son, Vietnam veteran, widower, returns to the village he was born in but never lived in, buys back the ruined house his father was forced to sell, and earns the right to stay by bringing the old family wrong into the open and refusing the fight everyone expects of the American veteran. Agata Lo Verde, keeper of the village's oldest grudge across the terrace wall, calls him by his name at the end. Source page: the treatment 05-development-decisions/concept-development-2026-06-14.md (CANON.md is a stub). All character and place names carry the treatment's ⚑ Needs-Marco flags.
look: 1972 inland Sicily shot like 1970s Italian cinema: faded Eastmancolor warmth, heavy 35mm grain, mountain limestone, wheat gone gold and cut, olive and almond terraces, a single piazza, a church with a cracked bell. Found light only, per the Light Law: hard Mediterranean sun with no fill, deep doorway shadow, blown pale stone; interiors run on window slabs, bare work bulbs, hearths; one Brooklyn frame runs on airshaft daylight and a hallway bulb. Mixed color temperatures and faces falling into shadow are correct. Every frame full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars.

stills.notes: Treatment, 'The original premise' + Sequence A (Brooklyn, and leaving it): 'His mother's last clear request is a place name and a key that opens nothing she can remember.' The inheritance as a touch — her hands folded around his and the key. The whole film handed over in one held gesture; ref carries the lead's wardrobe only, no canonical face exists.
stills.prompt: A narrow bedroom in a railroad apartment off President Street, Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, 1972. Concetta Comparetto, small and fading against the pillows, presses an old iron key into her son's hands and folds both of hers around them, holding on. Sal Comparetto, twenty-six, a butcher's son, broad-shouldered, careful with his hands, sits on the edge of the bed with his head bowed over their joined hands, saying nothing. The room's light is what the airshaft gives: grey daylight through one lace-curtained window, cool on the bedclothes, and the warm tungsten spill of a hallway bulb through the half-open door across the linoleum, two temperatures meeting on the blanket. Faces fall into shadow. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Sequence A turn: 'he steps off the bus into Càlamonte and is named "u Bruculinu" by a stranger before he says a word.' The look held too long — a stranger who already owns his story. The title of the picture happening to his face; ref carries wardrobe and suitcase only.
stills.prompt: Early afternoon in Càlamonte, a stone village terraced into the flank of the Madonie mountains, inland Sicily, summer 1972. Sal Comparetto, twenty-six, white shirt and brown trousers, has just stepped off the country bus with his suitcase in one hand and a blanket-lined fruit crate under his arm, the bus's dust still hanging in the street behind him. From the shade of a doorway an old man in a flat cap has just spoken one word at him, and Sal has stopped mid-step, holding the stranger's eyes, named before he has said anything at all. Hard sun drops straight down the narrow street, blowing the pale stone out; the old man sits almost lost in doorway shadow, no fill anywhere. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, 'World and setting — The land': 'The Comparetto house is a roofless shell on a terrace above the village, sold under duress decades ago and since let go to ruin.' Paired with the key 'that opens nothing.' A man touching what his family lost — grief into roots, the spine of action met for the first time.
stills.prompt: Inside the roofless shell of the Comparetto house on a terrace above Càlamonte, Madonie mountains, inland Sicily, summer 1972. Sal Comparetto stands alone in what was the kitchen, one palm laid flat against the doorway stone the way a man touches a grave, his mother's iron key hanging useless from his other hand, head bowed. Open sky where the roof was. Weeds through the fallen masonry, a collapsed hearth, a fig sapling grown up between the floor stones. Hard noon sun comes straight down through the missing roof in one blown shaft across his shoulders and the doorway; everything the shaft misses drops into deep shadow. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Sequence B: 'meets Agata across the terrace wall (first sparks, all friction).' Character list: 'the one person who refuses to call Sal by the nickname and refuses to forgive on schedule.' The look held too long as open combat — the heart-line begins at a property line. 02-love-interest.png carries her face and curls only; her casting as Agata is an open ruling.
stills.prompt: Two terraces meet at a dry-stone wall above Càlamonte, Madonie mountains, inland Sicily, summer 1972. Sal Comparetto, twenty-six, white shirt with the sleeves rolled, has straightened up on his ruin's side of the wall; Agata Lo Verde, thirties, dark curls tied back, a work apron over her dress, has stopped dead on hers with a hay fork still in both hands. The look between them holds too long to be neighborly and too hard to be welcome, neither giving the first word. Morning sun rakes low across the terraces from the east, long shadows off the olive trees, her face half in shadow, his blown bright against the stone, no fill. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Sequence D: 'Slow thaw with Agata over a shared, practical necessity (water, a wall, a harvest). First real warmth.' Tone section owns the image: 'water in a channel... hands at work.' The thaw as hands almost touching in the same water — the emotion is the entire event of the frame.
stills.prompt: A stone water channel running between two terraces above Càlamonte, inland Sicily, late summer 1972. Sal Comparetto and Agata Lo Verde kneel on opposite banks clearing the channel together, both pairs of hands in the same running water, his and hers almost touching around the same lifted stone. She has just looked up at him and the sharpness has gone out of her face, the first warmth she has allowed him, and he has caught it and gone still. Late-afternoon sun comes low through the olive trunks behind them, blowing hot off the moving water, their faces lit by its bounce alone, the terraces beyond falling into shade. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Sequence F turn (all-is-lost): 'Sal is ready to sell the house back to Don Calò and leave, the way his father once did, repeating the family's defeat.' The packed suitcase against the crate-blanket he arrived with — father and son rhymed in one room, defeat as a posture, not an act.
stills.prompt: Night inside the half-rebuilt Comparetto house above Càlamonte, inland Sicily, 1972, new roof beams up but still open to the dark. Sal Comparetto sits on an overturned mortar bucket with his packed suitcase already standing at the door, elbows on his knees, face pressed into his hands, ready to sell the house back and leave the way his father left. On the new-laid floor in front of him sits the blanket-lined fruit crate he was carried out of Sicily in. One bare work bulb on a drop cord burns close overhead, the only light, hard and unshaded, throwing his shadow huge across the raw stone; through the unglazed window the few lamps of the village burn far below. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Sequence G + character list: 'Padre Ignazio gives Sal the documented truth of the old wrong (the parish record)' — the priest who 'holds, in the parish register and in his memory, the documented truth of what was done to the Comparetto land.' The wound nobody in Brooklyn would explain, landing on a face. Padre Ignazio is a ⚑ placeholder name.
stills.prompt: The sacristy of the village church of Càlamonte, its cracked bell silent above, inland Sicily, autumn 1972. Padre Ignazio, old and deliberate in his cassock, holds the parish register open on the vestment table, one finger resting on a line written decades ago, and watches Sal's face instead of the page. Sal Comparetto grips the table edge with both hands and reads the documented truth of what was done to his family, the thing nobody in Brooklyn would explain, arriving all at once behind his eyes. One small deep-set window throws a hard slab of daylight across the open register and the two men's hands; the vestments, the shelves, the priest's shoulders fall away into darkness. Full-bleed edge to edge, no black bars. 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Sequence H: 'Agata calls Sal by his name for the first time. The final image rhymes the opening: the crate-blanket his parents carried him out in, now laid in the home he chose.' The whole arc resolved in a word and a turn of the head; the romantic resolution itself (married, betrothed, open) is a flagged ⚑ Marco ruling, so the frame stops at the name.
stills.prompt: Autumn 1972, the doorway of the finished Comparetto house above Càlamonte, inland Sicily, the roof tiled, the terrace worked and cleared. Agata Lo Verde stands just outside the open door and has just called Sal by his name for the first time. Sal Comparetto, a trowel still in one hand, has turned in the doorway to look at her, caught, the word still landing on him, the beginning of a smile he does not yet trust. Behind him inside, the blanket-lined fruit crate he was carried out of Sicily in sits on a chair by the finished hearth. Low autumn sun rakes up the terrace and lights her back and his face; the room behind him keeps its own shadow.
